messages:
carla: Quick sync — PRD checkpoint for Nimbus Health rollout. Need to lock must-have vs nice-to-have before we hand to Eng. TL;DR: customer requires deterministic latency <=300ms median for chat, soft requirement on throughput, and data isolation (dedicated).
ben: Reading now. two immediate questions: 1) do we commit to model quantization for launch? 2) rollout cadence (canary % and decision gates)?
anya: For quality baseline, we should run the 1k prompt eval set we used for Dedicated beta. Target: no more than 1.5% drop in our internal eval score vs current prod model. If quantizing, include eval with 8-bit and int4 variants.
mike: Ops constraints: Dedicated pool can be provisioned but autoscale lead time ~24h. For canary we should avoid >10% traffic until autoscale verified. Also need clear rollback automation triggers.
carla: Proposed scope (MUST): tenant pinning (per-tenant model), canary staged rollout, rollback automation, acceptance tests + smoke eval set, and simple telemetry dashboard. NICE: per-tenant routing policies, multi-quantization profiles, advanced A/B with UI.
ben: Agree. For rollout strategy I propose staged canary + A/B variant run-in-parallel for signal collection. Suggested gates:
- safety: no error spike (5xx increase) > 0.5% absolute
- latency: p95 under 500ms for canary (target 300ms in prod)
- quality: eval delta <=1.5% on Nimbus eval set
- business: conversion metric no drop >3% after 24h
anya: Add automated inference-level checks: token perplexity baseline + a few hand-curated prompts from the customer to detect hallucination mode.
carla: Here's a config snippet for the rollout we can iterate on:
```
rollout:
  strategy: staged_canary
  stages:
    - pct: 5
      duration: 2h
    - pct: 20
      duration: 6h
  experiments:
    - type: shadow_a_b
      compare_with: prod
  pinning: tenant
  rollback_criteria:
    - 5xx_rate_increase > 0.5%
    - latency_p95 > 500ms
    - eval_score_drop >= 1.5%
  automatic_fallback: model:v1.9-quantized
```
ben: Two implementation notes: 1) make the rollout engine emit a "gate-eval" snapshot after each stage (tokens + perf + eval delta) 2) pin expiry default = 7 days (customers can extend).
mike: We'll implement the gate-eval webhook to call the QA runner and push results into the rollout dashboard. If any gate fails, eng-bot will trigger rollback with a short message.
eng-bot: deploybot: Canary rollout started for nimbus-health (stage 1: 5% traffic) — watching gates.
anya: Edge cases we need explicit acceptance criteria for: warmed vs cold KV cache (measure on cold start), token-length distribution mismatch (long-tail requests), and fallback correctness (ensure kv-cache compatibility with fallback model).
carla: Acceptance criteria draft (finalizable):
- functional: tenant pinning routes 100% of chosen tenant traffic to pinned variant within 30s of config push
- perf: median latency <=300ms, p95 <=500ms on staged traffic
- quality: eval delta <=1.5% on Nimbus eval set, no critical hallucinations on curated prompts
- reliability: automated rollback triggers must succeed end-to-end in test env
- ops: documented runbook, runbook drill completed with SRE
ben: I'll put together a short RFC PR with the above and an action list. Can we aim to freeze MUST scope by EOD tomorrow so Eng can size?
carla: Yes — please comment on the PR with gaps. @mike can you confirm autoscale provisioning ETA?
mike: Confirmed — provisioning window 24–30h after commit. I'll queue capacity after scope freeze.
carla: Awesome. If no blockers, plan: freeze scope -> eng RFC -> dev spike (quantized eval) -> canary next week. :thumbsup:
ben: :thumbsup:
anya: :thumbsup:
eng-bot: deploybot: Canary stage metrics: p95=420ms, 5xx_rate delta=+0.1%, eval_delta=0.9% (within gates) — continuing monitoring.
